rv.q: Now on view in a superbly acted production at Woolly Mammoth Theatre, Posner's world premiere imagines a group of Jewish artists holed up in an office to work on a script their agent hopes will be a Hanukkah-themed smash.
Despite the story strands that never make sense and thanks to the actors, Hanukkah Spectacular is well-assembled theatre.

In the end, Hanukkah Spectacular reveals that true discomfort is not offensive material on a written page, but the quiet ache of a man who is lost—unmoored from his faith, his family, his career, and any real sense of identity

There is excitement in a new play willing to wrestle with complicated questions, and the cast’s considerable talent keeps the production engaging even when the material gets a little tangled in its own ambitions.
Hanukkah Spectacular is repetitive, elliptical and ultimately a shrug.

cn.t: Critics are split on Max Posner's *Hanukkah Spectacular*, with universal praise for its superb ensemble but divided opinions on the script's ambition vs. coherence. Some find it brilliantly discomforting; others say it's not quite ready.
